__doc__: Maintained by session-start-prep.py + session-end-flush.py + check-iteration-trigger.py + user-prompt-inject.py + maintenance_workorder.py (all writes go through _state_io's lock/atomic-replace/three-way-merge). heartbeat-check.py and memory-ask.py READ it only. Drives dormant/wake-up detection, memory decay gating, pending_maintenance state, summary drift repair history. recent_drift_repairs (v0.2.2): ISO timestamps of recent SessionStart drift repairs in last 30d, used by C+ drift check to detect SessionEnd timeout patterns. DEPRECATED: weighted_events_since_last_iteration is kept for backward compatibility only — check-iteration-trigger.py recomputes weights in real time from events.jsonl and does not read or update this field.

__pending_maintenance_schema__.__doc__: Field contract for each pending_maintenance entry. Written by check-iteration-trigger.py upsert_pending(); GC'd by session-start-prep.py after status=closed + closed_at older than PM_CLOSED_RETENTION_DAYS. Kept here (not in prose docs) so the contract ships with the plugin and stays machine-checkable.
__pending_maintenance_schema__.kind: signal category, e.g. problem_threshold / cadence_timeout / memory_backlog / close_check_due
__pending_maintenance_schema__.dedup_key: stable identity WITHOUT a time component — a time-bearing key piles up synonymous entries while the condition stays unresolved
__pending_maintenance_schema__.closed_at: ISO-8601 or null. NOT just an audit stamp: this timestamp IS the scoring baseline for the entry's own dedup_key — dismissing a signal means the user judged every piece of evidence before that moment closed out, so check-iteration-trigger.py restarts that kind's count from here (dismissal_baseline(); per dedup_key, closing one kind never affects another). Three shapes: evidence-filter kinds (problem_threshold / activity_threshold / close_check_due) only count evidence whose ts is > closed_at — events.jsonl entries for the first two, each stale entry's last_marked_at for the third; date-baseline kinds (cadence_timeout / completed_delta) move their start date past it, and never backwards (cadence takes whichever is later, the dismissal or the last iteration); the suppression-window kind (memory_backlog) is skipped wholesale while a non-GC'd closed entry exists — it scans current notes state, so there is no evidence timestamp to compare and no separate constant to tune. Consequences: never hand-edit it, and keep PM_CLOSED_RETENTION_DAYS == EVENTS_WINDOW_DAYS and >= CADENCE_DAYS (validate: pm_retention_matches_events_window) — this entry is the only carrier of the suppression, so its GC deadline is how long the suppression lasts.
